candidates.name: Extramammary Paget Disease
support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla with progressive infiltration of the overlying skin and the histopathological findings are consistent with Extramammary Paget Disease

candidates.name: Apocrine Gland Tumor
support_spans: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
candidates.why: The presence of apocrine glands in close association with the tumor cells and the positive immunohistochemistry for GATA3 and estrogen receptor suggest an apocrine gland tumor
